evals.prompt: What's new in cs.CL today? Give me like 5 papers.
evals.expected_output: Calls research_arxiv_list_top_n for cs.CL with n=5, presents a compact list (title, authors, submission date, arxiv_id) with abstracts, and fetches no full text.
expectations: Calls research_arxiv_list_top_n with include_categories=["cs.CL"] and n=5
Each listed item shows title, authors, submission date (published), and arxiv_id
Every item's abstract is shown, verbatim if 300 words or fewer, condensed to 300 words or fewer otherwise
No full text is fetched or written to .prioris/papers/ at any point

evals.prompt: Give me separate digests for cs.LG and stat.ML, but exclude anything already in stat.ML from the cs.LG one.
evals.expected_output: Two separate per-category digests via two separate research_arxiv_list_top_n calls, with the cs.LG call excluding stat.ML, using the default count since none was specified.
expectations: Makes two separate research_arxiv_list_top_n calls, one for cs.LG and one for stat.ML, rather than one combined intersection call
Uses the default n=7 since no count was specified
Presents the two digests separately rather than merging them into one list

evals.prompt: Daily digest for q-bio.NC — what's trending?
evals.expected_output: Treats 'trending' as 'most recent' (arXiv has no citation/trending signal), uses the default count, and does not fabricate any ranking metric.
expectations: Calls research_arxiv_list_top_n with include_categories=["q-bio.NC"] and the default n=7
Does not present or invent a citation count, trending score, or popularity ranking
Notes, plainly, that results are ordered by recency rather than a trending signal since arXiv doesn't expose one
